findings.evidence: Verifier probe with only jsonschema 4.26.0 and referencing 0.37.0, standalone field, B1 base: schema {"type":"object","properties":{"n":{"multipleOf":0.5}}}. check_schema passes; Draft202012Validator.iter_errors({"n": 10**400}) raises OverflowError (jsonschema/_keywords.py multipleOf computes instance / dB before its try block). validate_mcp_descriptor accepts the descriptor; rendering the same field from a restored release returns it. Read literally, RITORNO-AL-PROGETTO section 2 ('dove ... falliscono su un'istanza, il profilo rifiuta') and verifier control 1 would make this blocking. I classify it non-blocking: section 2 and the decided REM-0063-CYCLE13-EVALUATION-CONTEXTS (A1/B1) scope the static rule to reference resolution and non-progressing evaluation, and the contract (README:444, 'A library resolution exception on an instance requires refusal'; README:1025, 'The A1/B1 static checks cover resolution and progress') records that boundary. The failure depends on the magnitude of the instance, not on the schema structure. Refusing every float multipleOf would be a new normative semantic that no PO decision covers. No resolution- or recursion-related counterexample was found (see commands).
findings.required_fix: Open one decision request so the PO confirms the boundary. The matrix dimension to add or exclude is: numeric keyword with a float divisor (multipleOf) x instance outside the float range (and NaN). If the PO confirms the exclusion, record in the contract that non-resolution library failures caused by out-of-range instance values are outside section 2, with this example. If the PO includes them, add that dimension to the matrix and refuse the class on both public paths.
